subject: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, PeopleOps Consulting <ops@peopleops.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms

Hi team,

Now that Q3 close is behind us, I'd like to lock the high-level plan for the 2026 annual performance review cycle. Goal: clear timelines, a single manager form set, calibration windows, and a short, transparent comms cadence (managers -> ICs).

Must-haves:
- Firm dates for manager self-review, peer feedback window, calibration, and final ratings
- A consolidated manager form (one PDF/Doc) — we should avoid multiple templates this year
- Draft comms for managers and ICs (two versions: concise, and FAQ)
- HR/PeopleOps review for any policy changes and legal sign-off on promotion language

Attached: a draft calendar and a first-pass manager comm draft (manager-communication-draft_v1.docx).

Questions for this thread:
1) Monica — can PeopleOps guarantee we can compress peer feedback to 7 business days without losing participation?
2) Mina/Laura — any major conflicts with product shipping/cycle or leadership offsites in Nov/Dec?
3) Rishi — should calibration be split by org (Engineering, Product, Sales) or combined?

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Oct 4: manager forms finalized and posted
- Oct 11–18: manager self-reviews and peer nominations
- Oct 19–29: peer feedback window (7–8 business days)
- Nov 1–10: calibration rounds
- Nov 15: leaders finalize ratings and comp recommendations
- Nov 22: comms to managers; Nov 29: comms to all employees

I know this is tight; trying to avoid performance conversations overlapping heavy holiday weeks. Please reply with redlines by EOD Mon Oct 4.

Thanks,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: 2026-review-calendar.xlsx, manager-communication-draft_v1.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, PeopleOps Consulting <ops@peopleops.com>, olivia.franklin@payroll-partner.com
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms

Thanks Avery — good starting point. A few notes from PeopleOps and payroll coordination: 

1) Peer window compression: PeopleOps (Kate) confirms a 7-business-day peer feedback window is feasible if we send reminders on day 3 and day 6 and keep the form under 10 minutes to complete. We recommend a short reminder script for managers.

2) Forms: we'll consolidate into a single manager evaluation doc (see attached calibration-guidelines.pdf). We'll include standardized prompts for promotion readouts to streamline comp packet prep.

3) Calibration structure: recommend two waves — a role/discipline-level pre-calibration (smaller groups) followed by a cross-org calibration for final alignment. This reduces noise and shortens senior leadership time. Proposed: Nov 1–5 for pre-calibration; Nov 6–10 for cross-org.

4) Payroll timing: Olivia notes comp changes must be submitted by Nov 19 to hit December payroll. That pushes the leader finalization date to Nov 15 at latest — your schedule accounts for that.

5) Comms: attached is a manager comms draft and a short employee FAQ. Please keep promotion language consistent with prior years to avoid legal review delays; we'll highlight any required changes.

I've attached an updated calendar (2026-review-calendar.xlsx) with these shifts and a clean manager-comm draft (manager-communication-draft_v2.docx).

Monica Patel
Senior People Partner, PeopleOps
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-review-calendar.xlsx; manager-communication-draft_v2.docx; calibration-guidelines.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms

Agree with Monica on the two-wave calibration. A couple of practical flags from the leadership side: 

- Engineering has two major ship/launch windows Oct 25–Nov 2 and Nov 16–22. The pre-calibration dates (Nov 1–5) overlap the first window. Can we nudge pre-calibration earlier by 2 days (Oct 29–Nov 3) or run a condensed pre-calibration session for engineering leads?

- For managers who have direct reports in multiple regions, recommend time-block guidance in the comms so managers can schedule short 30–45m one-on-ones within two weeks of receiving final ratings. If Nov 15 finalization holds, that leaves a tight window before holidays.

- Calibration attendance: ask that each calibration group sends one senior leader plus one manager for context. This keeps sessions lean.

I'll work with my managers to gather schedule conflicts and share a consolidated list by Wed (Oct 7).

Rishi
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:54:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms

Thanks all — two quick comms suggestions from Product: 

1) Manager comm template: add a short bullet section with "How to handle edge cases" (e.g., leaves of absence, recent transfers, role changes mid-cycle). That should reduce ad-hoc HR escalations.

2) FAQ: include an explicit question on "What if I disagree with my manager's rating?" to set clear next steps and timelines — managers get a script to follow.

Also flagged: our Nov 18–19 leadership offsite (global product summit). If calibration requires a cross-org meeting that week, we should ensure priority representation or move the cross-org window to Nov 6–10 as Monica proposed.

Mina
Director, Product Management

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: PeopleOps Consulting <ops@peopleops.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning: 2026 annual performance cycle — timelines, forms, and comms

Appreciate the quick feedback — this thread gives me confidence we can make the timeline. Actions and owners: 

- Monica/PeopleOps: finalize forms, add "edge cases" section to manager comms, and publish calendar by Oct 4 (owner: Monica).
- Rishi: compile engineering scheduling conflicts and suggest a condensed pre-calibration plan if needed (owner: Rishi).
- Mina/Laura: review manager comm script and FAQ; provide edits by Oct 7 (owners: Mina, Laura).
- Avery: consolidate final timeline and reserve calibration meeting blocks Nov 1–10 (owner: Avery).

I'll update the Confluence playbook and link the final materials (see related links). If there are any absolute blockers to the Nov 15 finalization date (payroll cutoff), flag immediately to Monica and cc me.

Final note: please keep all comms to managers unchanged until PeopleOps gives the approved package — want a single source of truth.

Thanks everyone — I'll circulate the consolidated plan tomorrow morning.

Avery
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
